result.title: LiNO: Lightweight Network for Occupancy Estimation
result.summary: Occupancy estimation for automated vehicles is a crucial task that builds a 3D map using vehicle sensors. This map allows the vehicle to identify drivable areas and various obstacle classes. The task involves complex subtasks such as depth estimation, object classification, and segmentation to align semantic information with the 3D grid. Moreover, producing these estimations from multiple sensors demands significant computational power and memory, as high-dimensional data fusion requires complex feature extraction and processing. Consequently, most existing methods rely on large and computationally intensive architectures that are not suitable for real-time or real-world applications. We present a real-time, lightweight architecture that leverages camera and radar sensors through a residual multi-stage head. Unlike prior methods that rely on heavy camera-only blocks, our architecture employs camera-radar fusion and lightweight components. Additionally, we introduce a task-specific data augmentation strategy that enhances data diversity and improves generalisation. Our method achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance, attaining 45.7 mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) on Occ3D and 41.9 Ray-level Intersection over Union (RayIoU) (41.9) on OpenOcc datasets, running at 17.2 frames per second (FPS) and using only 5.3 GB of memory, compared with 4.1 FPS and 7.7 GB for STCOcc.
